correctness.rationale: The final claim is about homogeneous degree-five nonzero equations over F2, not abstract genus-six isomorphism types. Interpolation evaluation V_5 -> F2^7 is surjective, with each rational-zero pattern supported by 2^14 coefficient vectors. The Fano-plane action has ten subset orbits with multiplicities (1,7,21,7,28,7,28,21,7,1). Independent integer arithmetic gives sum multiplicity*per-subset smooth counts 688128 and blocking sum 242326, reducing to 17309/49152; 64 of 128 subsets are blocking. Correct geometric smoothness test: in characteristic two, Euler degree five gives F=sum X_i d_iF; the three degree-four derivatives form a homogeneous regular sequence iff their quotient has no projective support; regularity gives socle degree 9, so surjectivity (rank 66) of S6^3 -> S10 characterizes smoothness. Inspected both actual C++17 sources at the frozen Git tree: direct 2^21 enumeration using binary Gaussian elimination and independent GL3(2)-orbit enumeration using a different ordering/pivot method. The exhaustive 2^21 runs were NOT independently repeated in this execution; the supplied exact algorithms and their coverage, not merely saved output logs, were inspected. The 1516/2688 projective-orbit refinement requires those exhaustive runs and is consistent with established aggregate 4204. Finite domain is exhaustive by construction when programs terminate successfully; no claim for degrees/fields other than (5,F2).
